mini.assemble.desc: Tickets pile up; assemble right on the shelf: bowl → noodles (hot · rinse · hot again) → toppings in order → broth. 10 tickets, every step graded.
mini.reflex.title: ⚡ Reflex
mini.reflex.desc: FIXED topping grid like the real shelf · a dish name appears → tap all its toppings before time runs out · 10 in a row.
mini.scopeNote: pick dishes under Practice. Results count toward mastery, +10k per clean answer.
how.title: How to play · options
how.body: Tap to go. Topping shelf → take · blanching pot → drop noodles (3 baskets, they spoil if left) · noodles hot → cold rinse → hot · assembly counter → in order · ladle broth · carry to the table. ≥1★ unlocks the next day; money + tips buy kitchen upgrades and decor.
rep.title: Kitchen report — how to get faster
kitchen.far-pot.name: Pot at the far end
kitchen.left-topping.name: Toppings switched sides
kitchen.island.name: Island counter
level.pho-1.hint: Tap a shelf to take, tap the pot to blanch. Bowls are pre-scalded — take a bowl, add noodles, brisket and rare beef, ladle broth, carry to the table.
level.pho-2.hint: The shop's real order: brisket → rare beef → onion → coriander + sawtooth herb → scallion → ladle broth.
level.pho-3.hint: Take a bowl from the shelf → into the blanching pot → take the hot bowl out. Scald a few ahead when you're free.
level.pho-4.hint: Phở noodles: blanch hot → cold rinse at the sink → blanch hot again, then into the bowl. From here on it's the real shop process.
level.pho-5.hint: Three bowls at once: drop all 3 noodle baskets first, scald bowls ahead, then assemble one by one.
level.pho-6.hint: A basket rim turning red means the noodles are getting old. Spoiled ones go in the trash, never the bowl.
level.pho-7.hint: The kitchen changed today: the pot is at the far end. Do several things per trip.
level.pho-8.hint: Two people at one table — their bowls have to come out close together.
level.pho-9.hint: Only one basket: keep blanching nonstop, grab toppings while you wait. Goal: 4 bowls with no order mistakes.
level.pho-10.hint: Lunch crowd incoming. Cậu Hai is a regular — his speech bubble tells you what he wants.
level.pho-11.hint: Phở đặc biệt: meatballs go in a basket to blanch like noodles, plus tripe. Order: brisket → tripe → rare beef → meatballs → onion → herbs → scallion.
level.pho-12.hint: Two dishes, different toppings. Read the bubble over the customer before you grab anything.
level.pho-13.hint: The topping shelf is on the left today. Every route changed — replan.
level.pho-14.hint: Rain means few customers — scald bowls and noodles ahead, because they pour in once it stops.
level.pho-15.hint: One hand today: one item per trip. Walk less — prep ahead, batch your work.
level.pho-16.hint: Tái đập: take rare beef + ginger to the board and pound, then use it in place of plain rare beef.
level.pho-17.hint: Blanch only what you need. Spoiled noodles and trashed items both cost stars.
level.pho-18.hint: Beef rib into the microwave (runs in the background) → cut on the board → warm it. Remember the side bowl.
level.pho-19.hint: Gold-rimmed customers tip triple but get hungry fast. Watch out for someone changing their order mid-way.
level.pho-20.hint: The assembly counter is in the middle of the floor — walk around it. A group of 4 arrives mid-shift — prep a lot before they show up.
level.pho-21.hint: Chicken broth isn't ready: put chicken stock in the pot, add pho broth, then heat. Chop the poached chicken on the board while you wait. Size M only.
level.pho-22.hint: Two broths on the stove. Heat the chicken pot BEFORE anyone orders — don't let it go cold and then scramble.
level.pho-23.hint: Warm the beef stew on the stovetop (background), then top the bowl. Still ladle pho broth as usual. Size M only.
level.pho-24.hint: Rare beef and greens go on the stovetop for a stir-fry, then onto blanched phở, then ladle broth. Size L only.
level.pho-25.hint: All seven dishes. The stovetop has ONE spot — order your warming and stir-frying so it never jams.
level.bun-rieu-1.hint: Crab broth is pre-made on the broth shelf. Take a bowl, add bún, tomato, tofu, then ladle broth.
level.bun-rieu-2.hint: Order: tomato → rare beef → tofu → shrimp → ladle crab broth → scallion last.
level.bun-rieu-3.hint: Tap the burner, pick in order: crab stock → blood → portion of water, then Heat. Each pot makes ONE serving.
level.bun-rieu-4.hint: From here it's the full shop process: bún blanched hot → cold rinse → hot again; broth cooked one serving at a time.
level.bun-rieu-5.hint: During prep, cook 2–3 broth servings ahead — each pot makes just one.
level.bun-rieu-6.hint: The broth shelf holds only one serving. Ladle it out before cooking the next; don't stockpile.
level.bun-rieu-7.hint: The walk from the bowl shelf to the pot is longer — scald bowls in batches.
level.bun-rieu-8.hint: Slow but right: 6 bowls with no order mistakes is 3 stars.
level.bun-rieu-9.hint: One hand means more trips — plan the pickup order so you never backtrack.
level.bun-rieu-10.hint: Dì Ba is back from the market; bún riêu is her favorite. Once the rain stops they pour in — cook broth ahead.
level.bun-rieu-11.hint: Finished broth sits on the burner and blocks it. Take it out right away to cook the next serving.
level.bun-rieu-12.hint: A group of 4 all want riêu. Cook 4 broth servings and scald bowls before they arrive.
level.bun-bo-1.hint: Bún bò uses thick vermicelli, blanched hot just once (no cold rinse). Broth is ready on the shelf.
level.bun-bo-2.hint: Most toppings in the world: boiled pork, beef shank, brisket, pork sausage, crab cake, onion, Vietnamese coriander, scallion.
level.bun-bo-3.hint: Tap the burner: bún bò broth → blood → portion of water → Heat. One serving per pot.
level.bun-bo-4.hint: From here the full shop process. Remember to scald bowls ahead.
level.bun-bo-5.hint: Lots of toppings — take them in pairs: two per trip, assemble continuously.
level.bun-bo-6.hint: Finished broth sits on the burner and takes the spot. Take it out before cooking more.
level.bun-bo-7.hint: The topping shelf switched sides. With this many toppings, your route matters more than ever.
level.bun-bo-8.hint: One wrong bowl resets the streak to 0. Slow down, read the order carefully.
level.bun-bo-9.hint: Gold-rimmed customer? Serve them first — triple tip.
level.bun-bo-10.hint: Thím Bảy is loud and likes it spicy. Busy lunch — cook 2 broth servings ahead.
level.bun-bo-11.hint: Short on gear today: one basket, one hand. Plan every trip.
level.bun-bo-12.hint: A group of 4 wants bún bò. Prep plenty of broth and bowls before they sit down.
level.hai-phong-1.hint: Bún cá Hải Phòng: tomato, fried fish, then ladle fish broth. Everything is pre-cut, just grab and use.
level.hai-phong-2.hint: Order: tomato → blanched water celery → fried fish → fish cake → scallion → ladle fish broth → dill last.
level.hai-phong-3.hint: Fish broth: fish stock → portion of water → Heat. Quick-blanch the water celery in the pot.
level.hai-phong-4.hint: Take 2 pieces of fish cake to the board and halve them into 4. Cut dill into 3, add after the broth.
level.hai-phong-5.hint: During prep: cut fish cake and dill, cook the broth ahead.
level.hai-phong-6.hint: The board sits on the topping shelf, so it switched sides too.
level.hai-phong-7.hint: Common mistake: dill before the broth. Dill always goes last.
level.hai-phong-8.hint: Water celery also gets blanched in the pot — with one basket, take turns.
level.hai-phong-9.hint: Bánh đa cua: bánh đa → blanched water spinach → fish cake → shrimp → tomato → onion → scallion → cracklings → fried shallots → ladle crab broth.
level.hai-phong-10.hint: Fish broth and crab broth share a shelf. Tapping the shelf asks which one you want.
level.hai-phong-11.hint: Only one broth serving fits — cook the kind the waiting customer needs, never extra.
level.hai-phong-12.hint: Noodles, water spinach and water celery all go through the pot — do several things per trip.
level.hai-phong-13.hint: Ông Năm has less patience than regular customers — his bowl first.
level.hai-phong-14.hint: Blanch exactly what's needed. Cooking the wrong broth also counts as waste.
level.hai-phong-15.hint: A 9-step dish with one hand — plan the pickup order so you don't backtrack.
level.hai-phong-16.hint: A group of 4 orders a mix of both dishes. Cook both broths ahead.
level.mon-kho-1.hint: Take a tray + liner paper from the bowl shelf, line it first. Dry dishes get no broth.
level.mon-kho-2.hint: Herbs first, bún next, 3 cucumber slices AFTER the bún.
level.mon-kho-3.hint: Dry dish, but the bún still gets blanched in the pot — it spoils if left.
level.mon-kho-4.hint: Kent confirmed: tray bún is also blanched hot → cold rinsed → blanched hot again.
level.mon-kho-5.hint: During prep: line a few trays, blanch bún ahead.
level.mon-kho-6.hint: The dry-noodle bowl is different from a soup bowl: take from the shelf, DON'T scald. Lettuce, cucumber and pickles are cut together on the board.
level.mon-kho-7.hint: Bún gà nướng is built just like bún nem cua — spot the pattern and you're faster.
level.mon-kho-8.hint: All three dishes need bún — blanch a big batch, then assemble in a run.
level.mon-kho-9.hint: Easy mix-up: trays go herbs then bún; dry bowls go bún first, then the cut salad.
level.mon-kho-10.hint: Út Mười loves photographing the bún chả tray — make it pretty.
level.mon-kho-11.hint: Bún đậu tray: liner → bún → lettuce → balm → mint → perilla.
level.mon-kho-12.hint: One basket and four dishes all need bún — keep blanching, never leave the pot empty.
level.mon-kho-13.hint: The herbs are across the room now — gather them in one trip.
level.mon-kho-14.hint: A plate in progress for that customer keeps — someone later will order the same dish.
level.mon-kho-15.hint: Four herbs with one hand — know the order so you don't backtrack.
level.mon-kho-16.hint: Bánh hỏi tray: bánh hỏi first, scallion oil, cucumber, mango, then bún, herbs, grilled pork last.
level.mon-kho-17.hint: Five dishes now — read the bubble carefully before lining a tray or taking a bowl.
level.mon-kho-18.hint: Blanch exactly what the waiting customers need.
level.mon-kho-19.hint: Walk around the counter — pick your direction before you tap.
level.mon-kho-20.hint: A group of 4 orders everything. Line trays, take dry bowls, blanch bún ahead.
level.chao-1.hint: No noodles in cháo. Today the porridge is pre-ladled and the dough stick pre-cut — just plate it.
level.chao-2.hint: Porridge is pre-heated on the shelf, bowls pre-scalded. Cut the dough stick on the board, ladle porridge, top with the pieces.
level.chao-3.hint: Tap the burner, pick cháo lòng, then Heat. Each pot makes one bowl.
level.chao-4.hint: From here the full process. Porridge takes time — heat it before customers arrive.
level.chao-5.hint: Three bowls means three pots. Heat them all during prep.
level.chao-6.hint: Cháo sườn is made like cháo lòng — just pick the right porridge at the burner.
level.chao-7.hint: Tapping the broth shelf asks which kind. Check the customer's bubble first.
level.chao-8.hint: Heat the kind that's needed, ladle it out, then heat the next.
level.chao-9.hint: Ladling cháo lòng for someone who ordered cháo sườn counts as a mistake.
level.chao-10.hint: Porridge is the slowest thing in the kitchen — heat plenty before lunch.
level.chao-11.hint: Finished porridge sits on the burner and takes the spot. Ladle it out right away.
level.chao-12.hint: The board sits on the topping shelf, so it switched sides too.
level.chao-13.hint: Gold-rimmed customers won't wait long — only take them if porridge is already on the shelf.
level.chao-14.hint: The rainy lull is exactly when to heat both porridges ahead.
level.chao-15.hint: One hand: bowl, porridge, dough stick are three trips. Heat and cut everything first.
level.chao-16.hint: Four bowls at once = four pots. Heat them from the start of prep.
level.khai-vi-1.hint: Starters go on a long plate. Today the spring rolls are fried and cut — take a plate, add the rolls.
level.khai-vi-3.hint: After frying, take them to the board and cut diagonally, then plate.
level.khai-vi-4.hint: Fryer: add 2 spring rolls, deep-fry on low (background) → board, cut diagonally → plate.
level.khai-vi-5.hint: Frying takes the longest — get the fryer going from the start of prep.
level.khai-vi-6.hint: Dip rice paper at the sink → board: 2 slices of boiled pork side by side → 4 shrimp → bún on the pork → fold 2 edges → 2 lettuce leaves → roll, halve, plate on the long plate.
level.khai-vi-7.hint: Spring rolls fry (wait in background), summer rolls are rolled by hand. Load the fryer first, then go roll.
level.khai-vi-8.hint: Wrong order ruins the roll: pork → shrimp → bún → fold → lettuce.
level.khai-vi-9.hint: The rice-paper sink and the board are now at opposite ends — plan the route.
level.khai-vi-10.hint: The fryer is the bottleneck. Keep it frying, roll summer rolls while you wait.
level.khai-vi-11.hint: Summer rolls need lots of things — with one hand, go in the right order.
level.khai-vi-12.hint: A plate in progress keeps for the next customer who orders that dish.
level.khai-vi-13.hint: To catch big spenders, always have a batch frying.
level.khai-vi-14.hint: Don't roll or fry extra when nobody has ordered.
level.khai-vi-15.hint: Six rolling steps with one hand — know the order and you're through.
level.khai-vi-16.hint: A group of 4 orders starters — fry and roll ahead before they arrive.
level.cha-ca-1.hint: Chả cá Lã Vọng is a tray of many little cups. Today they're pre-made — just plate: shrimp paste, lime, peanuts.
level.cha-ca-2.hint: Add the red chili cup and the herb cup (balm, perilla, mint).
level.cha-ca-3.hint: All 7 parts: shrimp paste → lime → peanuts → chili → herbs → dill plate → fish pan.
level.cha-ca-4.hint: From here you make them: shrimp paste cup with scallion oil, pick herbs into the herb cup, plate dill + scallion root + onion, put onion + dill in the fish pan.
level.cha-ca-5.hint: Work by type: make 3 shrimp paste cups in a row, then the next cup.
level.cha-ca-6.hint: No fixed order in this dish — just be neat and fast.
level.cha-ca-7.hint: Every cup is made on the board — when the board switches sides, the whole route changes.
level.cha-ca-8.hint: Seven parts with one hand — plate each cup as you finish it.
level.cha-ca-9.hint: Priciest dish in the shop, and big spenders tip triple — do theirs first.
level.cha-ca-10.hint: Make cups ahead when it's quiet.
level.cha-ca-11.hint: Make just enough — extra cups with no customer are waste.
level.cha-ca-12.hint: Four trays at once is 28 parts. Prep from the start, work by cup type.

trip.hn-hp.bubble: A traveler, huh? Come in — want to learn bánh đa cua, help me for a shift.
trip.hp-hue.title: HUẾ
trip.hp-hue.bubble: Long way, kid. Come in, I'll show you how a proper pot of riêu is made.
trip.hue-dn.title: ĐÀ NẴNG
trip.hue-dn.bubble: Still fixing the place up — come back another day.
trip.dn-nt.title: NHA TRANG
trip.dn-nt.bubble: Still fixing the place up — come back another day.
trip.nt-sg.title: SÀI GÒN
trip.nt-sg.bubble: Welcome to Sài Gòn! Mornings start with hot cháo — come help me cook.
trip.sg-mientay.title: MEKONG DELTA
trip.sg-mientay.bubble: Still fixing the place up — come back another day.
quan.pho.greet: Quit your job to learn cooking? Bold. Phở is lesson one — make a decent bowl before you talk about the road.
quan.pho.dare: Work the shift properly. Earn the stars and I'll give you the real recipe to take home.
quan.mon-kho.greet: You're the one who quit the office to learn cooking? I follow you online!
quan.mon-kho.dare: Bún chả and bún đậu trays have to look good for the photo. Herbs first, bún after — remember.
quan.cha-ca.greet: This shop is a hundred years old, kid. Chả cá has no fixed order, but all seven parts must be there.
quan.cha-ca.dare: Be neat, be quick. I'm not in a hurry, but the customers are.
quan.hai-phong.greet: Made it to Hải Phòng, huh. Red noodles, fish cake, crab broth — port food has to be bold.
quan.hai-phong.dare: I drive all day, ten minutes for breakfast. Fast and right, kid.
quan.bun-rieu.greet: Came all the way from the north to learn riêu? Sit down, let me tell you how this pot is made.
quan.bun-rieu.dare: Crab stock, blood, water — in that order or the broth clouds. One slip and the whole pot is muddy.
quan.bun-bo.greet: Bún bò Huế must be spicy, must smell of lemongrass, must be red with annatto. Can you handle spicy?
quan.bun-bo.dare: Most toppings on this road. Remember them all and I'm impressed.
quan.chao.greet: Sài Gòn wakes early, kid. The porridge pot boils at four a.m.
quan.chao.dare: Porridge takes long — start before anyone orders. Make them wait and they're gone.
quan.khai-vi.greet: Summer rolls and spring rolls — every foreigner loves them. Learn these and you can go anywhere.
quan.khai-vi.dare: Roll tight, fry on low. Two jobs, two rhythms — do them side by side to keep up.
intro.1: 11 pm. The hundredth spreadsheet. The third cup of instant noodles this week. What am I doing?
intro.2: An old photo on the phone: the phở stall at the alley, the old lady ladling steaming broth. I used to love that smell.
intro.3: Next morning: a resignation letter on the desk, next to a pair of chopsticks. A backpack, a mat, and one reason — go learn to cook this whole country.
intro.4: From Hà Nội all the way south. Ask into every kitchen, work the line until the owner hands over the recipe. The trip begins.
